text:
maria: @channel CS-4281 reported by AcmeCorp — many 5xx/timeout errors hitting the hosted API since 16:03 UTC. Customer sees intermittent 502s and long tail latencies (~10s). Dashboard shows request_queue_depth spiking and continuous-batcher backlog growing. Can we triage?
ryan: looking... I can see a sharp increase in dequeue_latency and batcher_queue_length on pool gpu-p3-3 around 16:02. p95 token latency up to 9.8s. Logs show repeated \"dequeue timeout\" errors from the continuous-batcher.
jordan: tagging in infra — initial hunch: tenant burst + small requests causing lots of small batches and kv-cache churn. Any tenant id we can correlate?
maria: tenant_id=acme-tenant-73, spike corresponds to a large customer job that started at 16:01 (bulk embeddings). Support ticket has sample request headers. Repro steps attached to ticket.
ryan: grabbing a few logs:
```
2026-03-18T16:03:12Z batcher[pid=4123] WARN dequeue_timeout pool=gpu-p3-3 tenant=acme-tenant-73 queue_len=1823 pending_batches=410
2026-03-18T16:03:13Z gateway ERROR request_handler 502 upstream_timeout tenant=acme-tenant-73 path=/v1/generate
```
ryan: metrics: enqueue_rate doubled, kvcache_miss_rate jumped from 2% -> 48%, batch_size median dropped (more tiny batches). Continuous batching window configured to 10ms on this pool.
maria: customer says they sent a throttled fan-out; maybe a client bug but we still need mitigation.
jordan: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) apply temporary tenant rate-limit for acme-tenant-73; 2) increase batcher worker count on gpu-p3-3; 3) raise dequeue timeout to avoid immediate 502s while backlog drains. Which one should we try first?
sara: +1 on a quick tenant throttle and a short-term worker bump. Also add a circuit-breaker so the gateway rejects instead of 502-ing when backlog > safety threshold.
ops-bot: @deploy-bot starting config change: apply-tenant-rate-limit acme-tenant-73 60rps (dry-run=false)
ops-bot: update: rate-limit applied (change-id=chg-8842).
maria: applied. Customer reports reduced error rate to ~10% but still occasional tail 504s.
ryan: running a controlled worker bump: scaling batcher_workers for pool gpu-p3-3 from 12 -> 18. Monitoring logs...
ryan: after scaling, dequeue_latency dropped by ~40%, queue_len down to ~200 after 3m, error rate trending down.
jordan: opened an infra ticket to investigate why kvcache miss rate exploded — possible eviction storm when embeddings job kicked many different prefixes.
sara: documented repro steps in the support ticket and linked the runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/queue-backlog (runbook has commands and rollback steps). Add customer-facing note that we're applying temporary throttles.
maria: customer acknowledged, will run reduced job. We'll keep rate-limit for 30m then reassess.
ryan: postmortem action items (short): - add alert for kvcache_miss_rate > 20% + queue_len>1000 - consider adaptive batcher window widening under high enqueue_rate - implement per-tenant backlog thresholds with graceful 429 fallback - improve observability for small-batch volume
jordan: also adding a short term autoscale policy for batcher_workers on gpu-p3 pools when continuous-batcher queue_len > 500.
sara: I'll follow up with CS to coordinate customer message and ask for sample traffic pattern to repro in staging.
maria: thanks team. Leaving thread open for the 30m check-in and then we'll close if stable.
ryan: monitoring looks stable at 16:09 UTC — keeping watch.
ops-bot: deploy-bot change chg-8842 scheduled rollback at 16:39 UTC unless extended.
maria: closing check-in, will reopen if errors reappear.
